q: How much CO2 does making plaster of Paris emit per tonne?
title: Plaster of Paris CO2 per tonne
short: Heating gypsum drives off water to make plaster of Paris; that releases no process CO2, unlike limestone. The CO2 comes from the fuel that heats the calciner and from grinding electricity. Divide both by tonnes of plaster produced.
audience: Plaster of Paris and gypsum board makers

ul: Calciner fuel: coal, pet coke, biomass or gas, at IPCC defaults.

p: Some plants use gypsum from fertiliser plants. Treat it as a by product with its own allocation, and say so.

senseible: Senseible reads the plant's electricity bills (CEA grid factor 0.710 kg CO2 per kWh for FY 2024-25, CO2 Baseline Database version 21.0) and fuel invoices (IPCC 2006 defaults) into a fingerprinted Scope 1 and 2 record, the plant-level input to a per-unit figure. Bought-in materials go to the supplier evidence trail; product reports are self-declared drafts.
